result.title: Scaling Laws for Safety Probes
result.summary: Safety probes trained on a model's activations are a standard tool for monitoring language models in real time. Each time a new model is released or a new harm area needs to be monitored, the probe must be retrained, which requires new labels and a choice of probe architecture. Yet neither the model nor the labels tell us in advance how well the resulting probe will perform. Finding out requires training and comparing many probe configurations. In this paper, we ask whether probe performance can instead be predicted in advance from model size and the number of labels. Existing safety datasets are insufficient for this, as they are either limited in scale or already saturated. We therefore construct six new safety datasets of sufficient size and difficulty. On these datasets, we train two probe architectures on 20 base models from five model families, with 32 to $10^{6}$ labels for each model. We measure performance using probe error, defined as 1 - AUROC, where lower values are better. We find that probe error follows two simple scaling laws. First, the lowest probe error a model can reach falls as a power law in its size. Second, probe error decreases towards its floor as the number of examples increases; the slope increases as the target model size increases. Both laws hold across tasks, model families and probe architectures, and only their fitted constants differ. When fitted on the smallest models of a family, the laws predict the error of the next larger model to within 0.02 in 72% of cases. They also identify whether more labels or a larger model is the cheaper way to reach a target error in 73% of cases. Finally, they choose the probe architecture with an extra error of only 0.006 on average when they pick the worse one. These laws allow safety researchers to determine how to create the best probe for any given model and label budget.

AI.brief_summary: 该文构建六个规模与难度足够的安全数据集，在 5 个模型家族、20 个基座模型上以 32 到 10^6 个标签训练两类探针，发现以「1 - AUROC」定义的探针误差随模型规模呈幂律下降，并随标签数向该下界收敛，据此可预测探针性能并权衡「更多标签还是更大模型」。
AI.relevance_reason: LVR 中常用线性探针检验 latent 状态是否保留视觉细节或任务必要信息，该文的误差下界与标签—规模缩放规律可供核查探针结论是否受探针容量或标注预算限制；但研究对象是安全监控而非多模态推理，迁移需自行判断。
